boards.label: Plumbing
boards.title: Plumbing tripwires
boards.summary: 3 tripped, 9 on watch, of 15. Stage 0 of 4 — every ingredient, no event: the buffer is gone and a drain day is near.

gate.title: Stage 0 of 4 — every ingredient, no event: the buffer is gone and a drain day is near
gate.text: A seizure needs two ingredients in place — no buffer, and a drain day — and then runs through four stages: (1) a spike in overnight rates; (2) the spike stays, which rings the bell; (3) transmission into Treasuries and stocks, the meltdown path; (4) the Fed fails to act, the confidence-break path. Stage decides whether it is a plumbing story (2019 stopped at stage 2) or a market one (March 2020 reached stage 3 for ten days).

groups.title: The overnight market
groups.blurb: The domestic repo market: about $3 trillion a day, re-agreed every morning. Watch the days, not the level.

groups.title: The offshore dollar
groups.blurb: The eurodollar system: the same trade done abroad with a currency as the pawn, through the same dealers.

groups.title: The new floors
groups.blurb: The layers stacked on top since 2020, none of them backstopped.

groups.title: From episode to meltdown
groups.blurb: What decides whether a seizure stays a plumbing story or becomes a market one: how far it travels before the Fed acts.

tiles.name: SOFR against the Fed's rate
tiles.question: Is overnight cash costing more than the Fed pays banks to hold it?
tiles.trip: Red at +25 basis points over the rate on reserves outside a month-end, or SOFR above the Fed's standing-repo ceiling on any day. A spike that does not come back down the next day is the real thing.
tiles.reading: SOFR 3.90% on 2026-09-25, +0 bp against the rate on reserves (3.90%); ceiling 4.00%. Worst spread in the last five sessions +0 bp.
tiles.evidence: September 2019: 2% to 8% in a morning, the day after a tax date and a Treasury settlement drained cash together.

tiles.name: The Fed's repo window
tiles.question: Are banks borrowing from the Fed because private lenders won't lend?
tiles.trip: Red at $50 billion or more, or any sustained use on ordinary days. Amber at $10 billion on a day that isn't month-end.
tiles.reading: Fed overnight repo lending $0.0 billion on 2026-09-25; peak in the last ten sessions $0.1 billion. SRF usage returned to ~$0 intra-month after the Dec-2025/Jan-2026 year-end spike (peak $75bn); reserves stood at $3.04tn as of Sep 9 2026 with RMPs paused for a second month, suggesting comfortable but watch-worthy conditions at Sep-30 quarter-end.
tiles.evidence: The window is a ceiling only if banks will use it; stigma has kept it under-used, which is why spikes get past it.

tiles.name: The buffer
tiles.question: Is there spare cash left to absorb a shock?
tiles.trip: This lamp is the standing condition, not the event. It stays red while the reverse-repo buffer is gone, until the Fed's balance sheet is growing with the economy on purpose or the repo window is open to everyone.
tiles.reading: Reverse-repo balance $1 billion (peak $2,550 billion); bank reserves $2,930 billion, -21 billion over 13 weeks. Every dollar of Treasury settlement now comes straight out of reserves.
tiles.evidence: Nobody knows where scarcity begins; the Fed found it by accident in 2019.

tiles.name: The drain calendar
tiles.question: Is a day coming when cash leaves the banks all at once?
tiles.trip: Amber inside five business days of a quarter-end, month-end settlement, or tax date; the lamp is a calendar, not a reading. Red only in combination with the SOFR or window tiles.
tiles.reading: Next drain: Wednesday Sep 30 (quarter-end), 2 days away. Upcoming: Sep 30 (quarter-end); Oct 15 (mid-month coupon settlement); Oct 31 (month-end settlement); Nov 15 (mid-month coupon settlement).
tiles.evidence: 2019's spike and every quarter-end pop since late 2025 landed on these dates. Seizures do not happen on a random Tuesday.

tiles.name: Treasury market function
tiles.question: Can the basis trade be unwound without breaking the market?
tiles.trip: Red on a failed or badly tailed coupon auction, dealers refusing balance sheet, bond volatility (MOVE) above 140, or bid-ask spreads widening the way they did in March 2020. Amber with MOVE above 100.
tiles.reading: MOVE index 96. Sep 23 2026 $70bn 5-year auction priced at 5.033% with a 3.1bp tail (second-largest on record), bid-to-cover 2.212 (weakest since Dec 2018), primary dealers absorbed 15.8%.
tiles.evidence: March 2020: repo tightened, the basis trade could not roll, Treasuries were dumped, and the Fed bought $75 billion a day. Ten days start to finish.
tiles.source: Yahoo Finance ^MOVE; auction results via web check

tiles.name: Bank stress
tiles.question: Are the lenders worried about each other?
tiles.trip: Red on a spike in a large bank's default-insurance cost or discount-window borrowing above $50 billion. Amber above $10 billion, or if uninsured deposits start moving to money funds again.
tiles.reading: Discount-window primary credit $6.2 billion (week of 2026-09-23). No public evidence of discount-window draws or large-bank CDS spikes in Sep 2026; big-bank stocks fell after the Sep 16 Fed hike but JPMorgan raised its dividend 10% on Sep 15, signalling balance-sheet strength; deposit flight to MMFs not reported at stress levels.
tiles.evidence: March 2023: $42 billion left one bank in a day through an app. The next run will be as fast.
tiles.source: FRED: WLCFLPCL; bank CDS via web check

tiles.name: The dollar shortage gauge
tiles.question: Are foreigners paying extra to borrow dollars through swaps?
tiles.trip: Amber past -30 basis points outside a quarter-end; red at -60 and beyond, the dealers refusing to extend balance sheet. March 2020 reached -150 on the yen.
tiles.reading: EUR/USD 3m basis was approximately -16 to -20bp in mid-May 2026; at Sep 28 quarter-end, structural JPY basis pressure is building (Japan's $550bn US investment deal expected to push JPY/USD basis more negative) but no RED-threshold breach reported; best available indicative JPY 3m basis circa -25 to -35bp at quarter-end.
tiles.evidence: When the swap market seizes, foreign holders do not default — they sell Treasuries. An offshore funding problem becomes a Treasury problem in the same week.

tiles.name: The Fed's swap lines
tiles.question: Are foreign central banks drawing dollars from the Fed?
tiles.trip: Red at $50 billion drawn; amber at $5 billion. Any non-trivial draw means the private swap market has stopped working somewhere.
tiles.reading: Central-bank liquidity swaps outstanding $0.1 billion (week of 2026-09-23). Peaks: $580 billion in 2008, $450 billion in 2020.
tiles.evidence: The swap lines have worked every time they were used, for the fourteen countries that have them.

tiles.name: Japan and the carry trade
tiles.question: Is the largest source of swapped dollars being pulled home?
tiles.trip: Red on a yen move of more than 5% in a week against the dollar, or a surprise Bank of Japan hike. Amber at 3%, or while the hiking cycle runs.
tiles.reading: Yen 157.2 per dollar, +0.1% on the week (negative = yen surging). BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.25% on Sep 18 2026 (highest since 1995); hike was fully priced so no surprise; USD/JPY was at 157.69 on Sep 28 2026, down ~1.3% over past month but not a 5% weekly move; Oct hike talk building.
tiles.evidence: August 2024: the yen jumped and U.S. stocks fell 8% in three days on no American news.
tiles.source: Yahoo Finance JPY=X; BoJ via web check

tiles.name: The basis trade
tiles.question: How much of the Treasury market is held on overnight money?
tiles.trip: Red when the trade unwinds — Treasury selling into a falling market with the futures basis blowing out. Amber standing while it exceeds $1 trillion.
tiles.reading: Morgan Stanley estimates basis trade notional fell to ~$900bn as of late Sep 2026, down from $1.26tn at start of 2026, reflecting reduced arbitrage opportunity rather than forced unwind; OFR estimated hedge-fund long cash Treasuries at $2.0tn as of Aug 2026.
tiles.evidence: Central clearing (December for cash trades, June 2027 for repo) will force margin on the trade, capping its leverage — safer after, riskier during the changeover.

tiles.name: Central clearing changeover
tiles.question: Will the plumbing survive its own repair?
tiles.trip: Red on a delay announced under pressure, a clearing-house margin call that cascades, or dealers dropping smaller counterparties in the run-up. Green once both deadlines have passed cleanly.
tiles.reading: SEC confirmed on Sep 22 2026 it does not intend to extend Dec 31 2026 (cash) or Jun 30 2027 (repo) deadlines; two significant scope questions remain outstanding; largest implementation challenge is bilateral legal documentation; IIB extraterritoriality exemption still open.
tiles.evidence: The clearing house becomes the too-big-to-fail node: 2020 and the 2022 nickel blowup showed what a margin spiral looks like.

tiles.name: Stablecoins
tiles.question: How large is the new money-fund lookalike with no backstop?
tiles.trip: Red on a large issuer trading below par for more than a day, or total supply falling 10% in a week. Amber standing.
tiles.reading: Total stablecoin supply ~$303bn as of Aug 2026 (Allium); Solana chain hit record $17.3bn on Sep 25 2026; no major issuer trading below par; supply down ~4.5% from May 2026 peak of $322bn but well within normal drift, no 10%-in-a-week drop or depeg event reported.
tiles.evidence: 2022's Terra collapse and 2023's USDC break were the rehearsals, at a tenth of today's size.

tiles.name: Private credit
tiles.question: Has the newest shadow bank closed its doors?
tiles.trip: Standing red while large funds gate redemptions; green after a full quarter of redemptions met in full.
tiles.reading: Blackstone BCRED ($79bn) gated at 5% in Jun 2026 after $4.4bn Q2 redemption requests; Blue Owl OBDC II suspended repurchases entirely; Q2 2026 industry requests hit record 12.4% of NAV with only 38% filled, leaving ~$9.6bn unmet; secondary-market tender offers pricing at 15-30% discounts to NAV.
tiles.evidence: About $2 trillion of bank lending done outside banks, funded by insurers and bank credit lines, with no window. The decision lives on Standing Orders.

tiles.name: Transmission
tiles.question: Has the seizure reached the markets — Treasuries and stocks falling together, the dollar jumping?
tiles.trip: Red when 10-year Treasury prices and the S&P 500 fall together for three sessions with the dollar index up. Amber on the first such day.
tiles.reading: Current streak of sessions with yields up, stocks down and the dollar up: 1. 10-year 5.18% on 2026-09-24.
tiles.evidence: In 2019 the spike never left the repo desks; the Fed lent within 48 hours. In 2020 it reached the Treasury market in ten days and every margin call in the world landed the same week.

tiles.name: The Fed's response
tiles.question: Once a seizure starts, how fast does the Fed lend — and does it stop when the episode ends?
tiles.trip: Red if a seizure (SOFR 25 bp over the floor for three sessions) runs with no Fed operations. Amber while operations run; green when they end. Purchases that continue after the episode normalizes are step two on the fiscal dominance board.
tiles.reading: Fed operations under way. Fed paused Reserve Management Purchases for a second consecutive month through mid-Oct 2026 (Sep 14 announcement), citing $3.04tn in bank reserves as ample; ~$15.6bn in reinvestment purchases continue; SRF rate set at 4.0% per Sep 16 implementation note; no emergency repo ops.
tiles.evidence: The precedents are days: 48 hours in 2019, ten days in 2020, a weekend in 2023. The Fed has never failed to act on a repo seizure since 1987; the only way this goes red is if it is stopped from acting.
tiles.source: FRED: SOFR, IORB, RPONTSYD; web check

boards.label: Market
boards.title: US market tripwires
boards.summary: 2 tripped, 4 on watch, of 9. One of the three bear-market conditions is present, 1 on watch.

gate.title: One of the three bear-market conditions is present, 1 on watch
gate.text: A 20% decline has always needed one of three things: earnings stop growing, borrowing costs jump, or an outside shock does one of the first two. Any one can start a bear market. Two at once reliably finish one. Only the three trigger tiles count here.

groups.title: What starts a bear market
groups.blurb: The three conditions the gate counts.

groups.title: What decides how far it falls
groups.blurb: Not triggers — they set the size of the drop.

groups.title: What could flip a trigger
groups.blurb: Early warning for the top section.

tiles.name: Borrowing costs have jumped
tiles.question: Is the 10-year Treasury yield holding above 5%?
tiles.trip: Trips when the 10-year holds above 5% for more than a few days.
tiles.reading: 5.18% on 2026-09-24; 2 consecutive readings at or above 5%.
tiles.evidence: Rates, not earnings, are what has moved this year.

tiles.name: Stocks yield no more than bonds
tiles.question: Does the market pay you anything extra for owning stocks instead of Treasuries?
tiles.trip: Trips when the earnings yield falls to or below the 10-year yield.
tiles.reading: Forward P/E 19.3 → earnings yield 5.18% against a 10-year at 5.18%: premium +0.00 points.
tiles.evidence: Expensive markets don't fall because they're expensive; they fall when a trigger hits, and valuation decides how far.
tiles.source: FactSet-style estimate via web check; FRED

tiles.name: Earnings stop growing
tiles.question: Are company profits still rising, and are forecasts still going up?
tiles.trip: Trips when forecasts for the next quarter start being cut, or growth falls below 10%.
tiles.reading: Next-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth estimate 29.1%; revisions up. As of Sep 24, 2026, S&P 500 forward 12-month P/E is ~19.3x on $398.74 forward EPS; FactSet reports Q3 2026 estimated YoY earnings growth of 29.1% (up from 26.7% at June 30); 62% of S&P 500 companies issued positive Q3 EPS guidance, well above the 5-year average of 41%.
tiles.evidence: About half of this year's earnings growth comes from AI-infrastructure companies.

tiles.name: The average stock is already falling
tiles.question: Is the index rising on a few giant companies while most stocks fall?
tiles.trip: Watch at half the members below their own 200-day average; red at two-thirds, or when the index itself breaks its 200-day average.
tiles.reading: S&P 500 7,710 vs 200-day 7,210 (0 closes below). 55% of 501 members below their own 200-day average (counted). Equal-weight vs cap-weight over 60 sessions: -5.2%. As of Sep 25, 2026, S&P 500 at 7,742 is above its 50-DMA (7,636) and well above its 200-DMA (7,205); however, only ~49.9–56% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 200-DMA (most recent confirmed print ~49.9% in late May/early June, with a market recovery since), indicating the rally remains somewhat concentrated and below the 60% historical average.
tiles.evidence: Narrow leadership is how the last two bear markets began.
tiles.source: Yahoo Finance, all constituents; web check as fallback

tiles.name: Lenders are getting nervous
tiles.question: Are bond investors demanding more to lend to risky companies?
tiles.trip: Trips on spreads above 5%, a 1.5-point jump in 60 days, or a VIX that stays above 30.
tiles.reading: High-yield spread 2.80% (+0.01 pts in 60 days); VIX 14.2.
tiles.evidence: Credit usually cracks after rates and before earnings.

tiles.tag: Trigger: outside shock — any one of five
tiles.name: Outside shock
tiles.question: Has anything from outside the market hit hard enough to force earnings down or rates up?
tiles.trip: Trips the moment any one of the five below goes red.
tiles.reading: 0 red, 5 on watch, of five.
tiles.evidence: The market treats every oil rise as a rate rise; the financial-accident row matters most while every one of its ingredients is present.

subs.name: Energy
subs.reading: Brent $115 (2026-09-22); CPI 3.7% y/y (2026-08-01). Red at $120 or inflation above 4%.

subs.name: China, Taiwan, the trade truce
subs.reading: On Sep 23–24, 2026, Xi Jinping completed a state visit to Washington and Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed the US-China trade truce extended through January 10, 2027, with reciprocal tariff cuts on $60B of goods; Taiwan chip-export controls and arms sales ($14B package frozen) remain unresolved; analysts warn the truce could break down on new unilateral tariffs or Taiwan disputes. Red if the chip and rare-earth rules snap back, a Chinese bank is sanctioned, or Taiwan sees a quarantine.

subs.name: A financial accident
subs.reading: Japan's 10-year JGB yield hit 3.03% on Sep 15, 2026 (30-year high), prompting a historic joint US-Japan yen intervention in late July/early August 2026; the 10-year US Treasury yield touched 5.01% in September according to the AI circular-financing tracker; carry-trade stress is elevated but a disorderly unwind has not yet materialized — no large fund or lender failure confirmed. Yen -1.0% in 30 days. Red on a Treasury-market seizure, a carry-trade unwind, or a large fund or lender failing.

subs.name: Policy shock
subs.reading: On Sep 5, 2026, Trump, Vance, Bessent, and senior economic advisors publicly pressured new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh not to raise rates — an unusually broad pressure campaign — but Warsh proceeded with a 25bp hike on Sep 16, 2026; the debt ceiling is not an immediate constraint (next binding event estimated summer 2027); Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs in Feb 2026 adding legal uncertainty. Red on broad new tariffs, a Fed-independence fight, or a debt-ceiling standoff.

subs.name: Pandemic, cyberattack, disaster
subs.reading: Iranian state-sponsored hackers targeted US water, telecom, and energy infrastructure since late August 2026 (NBC News, Sep 2); the FBI confirmed water/wastewater utilities in at least 7 states reported incidents since July 27, 2026; no mass-casualty or market-disrupting event confirmed, but attacks are escalating in scope. No warning possible; red only when it happens.

tiles.name: The economy
tiles.question: Is a recession starting?
tiles.trip: Trips when unemployment rises half a point from its low (the Sahm rule), or claims jump.
tiles.reading: Unemployment 4.1% (2026-08-01), low 4.0%; Sahm indicator -0.07; jobless claims 4-week average 202,250 vs 52-week low 189,000.
tiles.evidence: Strong demand is why the Fed keeps raising.

tiles.name: The AI-cycle bell
tiles.question: Has the AI spending boom started to turn? (Mirrors the AI board.)
tiles.trip: Trips when the AI board's bell rings: spending growth slowing and rental prices falling at the same time.
tiles.reading: Half-lit. Spending growth: Green; chips easier: Red.
tiles.evidence: Because AI companies supply half of index earnings growth, that bell is the likeliest trigger for the earnings tile.

tiles.name: The Fed
tiles.question: Is the central bank tightening into a stretched market?
tiles.trip: Trips on a hike while the 10-year is above 5%, or a surprise at the next meeting.
tiles.reading: Fed funds target (upper) 4.00%, up from 3.75% 90 days ago. On Sep 16, 2026, the FOMC unanimously raised the federal funds rate by 25bp to 3.75%–4.00% — its first hike since 2023; the Sep dot plot shifted year-end projections to 4.1%–4.4%; futures markets as of Sep 25 price ~4.2% by December and ~4.8% by Sep 2027; the next meeting is October 27–28, 2026, where markets are split between a hold and another 25bp hike.
tiles.evidence: The last hiking cycle coincided with a 20%+ decline.
tiles.source: FRED; Fed communications via web check

boards.label: AI cycle
boards.title: AI cycle tripwires
boards.summary: 2 tripped, 4 on watch, of 8. The bell has not rung.

gate.title: The bell has not rung
gate.text: It rings when two things are true at once: the big buyers' spending growth is slowing, and computing time is getting cheaper to rent. Together they have led the crash by one to two quarters.

parts.name: Chips are getting easier to get

groups.title: What comes first
groups.blurb: The two signals that showed up a year before the 2000 crash.

groups.title: What rings the bell
groups.blurb: The two that together have led the crash by one to two quarters.

tiles.name: The buyers are borrowing to buy chips
tiles.question: Are Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta spending more than the cash their businesses generate?
tiles.trip: Trips when two of the four spend above their operating cash flow (trailing four quarters, cash capex only — leases excluded, so this understates).
tiles.reading: Trailing-year capex as a share of operating cash flow: Microsoft 0.63×, Amazon 1.07×, Alphabet 0.71×, Meta 0.69×. 1 above 1.0, 0 above 0.8.
tiles.evidence: Companies that spend all their cash and borrow the rest eventually slow down.

tiles.name: Nvidia is financing its own customers
tiles.question: Is the chip seller lending or investing in the companies that buy its chips?
tiles.trip: A structural condition, not a level — it stays lit until the circular deals unwind.
tiles.reading: As of Aug–Sep 2026, Nvidia's equity portfolio in AI customers reached $99B (Sep 4 CNBC), with ~$46B in direct stakes and $879B in multi-year purchase commitments traced in Bloomberg's circular-flow diagram; Nvidia also announced $500B in third-party financing partnerships with Wall Street asset managers on Aug 10, and the BIS named AI capex circular financing one of three top global financial stability risks in its June 2026 Annual Report.
tiles.evidence: Lucent and Nortel financed their own customers in 1999, a year before they collapsed.

tiles.name: Spending growth is slowing
tiles.question: Are the big buyers still raising next year's spending forecasts, or starting to talk about 'digestion'?
tiles.trip: Trips on the first cut to the growth rate — not the level — or the word 'digestion' on a call.
tiles.reading: Trailing-year capex growth: Microsoft +80% (was +58%); Amazon +61% (was +62%); Alphabet +98% (was +90%); Meta +71% (was +73%). As of Q2 2026 earnings (late July 2026), Amazon raised 2026 capex guidance to ~$220B, Alphabet to $195–205B, and Meta to $130–145B; Microsoft's ~$175B reflects a lease-accounting reclassification, not a spending cut — all four reaffirmed or raised guidance with no digestion or efficiency language. In Q2 2026, Google Cloud grew 82% YoY to $24.8B with a $514B committed backlog; AWS grew 37% YoY to $42.2B; Azure grew 43% YoY — all three accelerating relative to Q1 2026.
tiles.evidence: This is the bell. Historically it rings one to two quarters before the guidance cut everyone waits for.

tiles.name: Chips are getting easier to get
tiles.question: Are rental prices for AI computing falling, waitlists disappearing, inventory piling up?
tiles.trip: Trips on a sustained 20–30% drop in rental prices, or Nvidia inventory growing 25 points faster than sales.
tiles.reading: Nvidia inventory +111% vs sales +106% (quarter ended 2026-07-26); inventory days 119. As of Sep 13–27, 2026, H100 median on-demand price is ~$3.25–$3.84/hr (Mercatus/AIM trackers), down roughly 40–50% from early-2024 peak but with demand spikes tightening availability; B200 averages ~$6.39/hr across 12 providers with floor at $3.69/hr; direction over 90 days is flat-to-modestly-declining for H100, stable for B200. As of September 2026, all three DRAM suppliers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) describe 2026 HBM output as effectively committed/sold out; conventional DRAM contract prices surged 93–98% QoQ in Q1 2026 with further increases of 10–20%/month guided through year-end; new HBM capacity not expected until 2028–2029. On Sep 16, 2026, Silicon Data reported B200 residual value at 158% of original cost (58% premium); H100 used prices stable at $18K–$25K with strong resale demand and CoreWeave's 2022-vintage H100s immediately rebooked at 95% of original pricing — no distressed volume dumping observed.
tiles.evidence: In 2000 Cisco's inventory outran its sales two quarters before the crash — visible in the public filings.

tiles.name: Interest rates keep rising
tiles.question: Is the 10-year Treasury yield holding above 5%?
tiles.trip: Amber at 4.75%; trips at 5% sustained.
tiles.reading: 5.18% on 2026-09-24; 2 consecutive readings at or above 5%.
tiles.evidence: Higher rates make the borrowing in tile 1 more expensive and expensive stocks worth less on paper.

tiles.name: Lenders are getting nervous
tiles.question: Are bond investors demanding more to lend to the AI borrowers, and are the labs still raising money easily?
tiles.trip: Trips on spreads above 5%, a 1.5-point jump in 60 days, or a delayed or downsized AI-lab round.
tiles.reading: High-yield spread 2.80% (+0.01 pts in 60 days). Financing remains robust — Anthropic closed a $65B Series H in May 2026 at a $965B valuation and CoreWeave announced a ~$3B ATM offering and $3B in convertible notes on Sep 18, 2026 — but OpenAI delayed its IPO to 2027+, and Amazon's $50B commitment to OpenAI includes $35B conditional on milestones, introducing contingency risk in the largest deal.
tiles.evidence: Watch Oracle- and CoreWeave-type borrowers first; they are the leveraged link between the labs and Nvidia.

tiles.name: The stock is acting wrong
tiles.question: Has Nvidia broken below its one-year average price, or gone vertical?
tiles.trip: Trips on 10 straight closes below the 200-day average, or +35% in 30 sessions.
tiles.reading: $231 vs 200-day average $200; 0 closes below it; +3% over 30 sessions.
tiles.evidence: Picks-and-shovels stocks peak before their customers' spending does.

tiles.name: Oil
tiles.question: Is Brent crude high enough to force more rate hikes?
tiles.trip: Watch at $100, amber at $110, trips at $120.
tiles.evidence: Oil is the reason rates are rising.

boards.label: Fiscal
boards.title: Fiscal dominance tripwires
boards.summary: 0 tripped, 6 on watch, of 12. The Fed is on step one of four — pressure building toward step three.

gate.title: The Fed is on step one of four — pressure building toward step three
gate.text: The path from central bank to Treasury financier has four steps, each defensible on its own: bill purchases for reserve management; a crisis purchase that outlasts the crisis; political pressure to hold yields down; a stated ceiling. Step one is normal. Step two is the slope. Step three is the pressure. Step four is 1942.

parts.name: A crisis purchase that outlasts the crisis
Political pressure to hold yields down

groups.title: The four steps
groups.blurb: The gate counts these. Watch is a step being approached; red is a step taken.

groups.title: The market's verdict
groups.blurb: What the people holding dollar promises are doing about it, ahead of any announcement.

groups.title: The pressure on the Fed
groups.blurb: The arithmetic and the plumbing that push toward the next step.

tiles.name: Reserve purchases outgrow reserves
tiles.question: Is the Fed buying more than the plumbing needs?
tiles.trip: Red when the balance sheet grows more than $100 billion beyond the growth in bank reserves over 13 weeks, or when the Fed buys coupons rather than bills. Amber while bill purchases run.
tiles.reading: Fed total assets $6,748 billion, +12 billion over 13 weeks; bank reserves -21 billion over the same period. As of Sep 27 2026, the Fed has bought ~$215 bn in Treasury bills since Dec 2025 under Reserve Management Purchases (RMPs) explicitly labelled reserve management, not yield support; the Sep 16 implementation note says purchases may extend to Treasuries ≤3-yr maturity 'if needed,' and ~$15.6 bn more are scheduled through Oct 14 to replace rolling-off MBS.
tiles.evidence: Compare the Fed's total assets with bank reserve balances, both weekly on the H.4.1. Buying that outruns reserves is buying for the Treasury.

tiles.name: A crisis purchase that outlasts the crisis
tiles.question: Has the Fed bought bonds under a financial-stability banner and kept buying after the episode ended?
tiles.trip: Red if purchases begun in an episode continue after the episode's own indicators (repo rates, auction results) have normalized.
tiles.reading: No legacy crisis-era purchase programme is active; the Dec 2025 RMP programme is framed as routine reserve management, not a financial-stability intervention, and ON RRP usage has fallen to near zero, indicating money-market stress has fully normalised.
tiles.evidence: Every crisis purchase since 1987 was justified as temporary; 2008's became permanent. The tell is the second month.
tiles.source: Fed statements; H.4.1 via web check

tiles.name: Political pressure to hold yields down
tiles.question: Is the executive branch or the Treasury talking about long yields as something the Fed should manage?
tiles.trip: Red when the Treasury Secretary or the White House names the 10-year as a target in public, or when the Fed's independence is challenged in law.
tiles.reading: Around Sep 5 2026, 'the president, vice president, Treasury secretary and one of the president's senior economic counselors' all publicly urged the Fed not to raise rates; Trump has not named a specific 10-yr or 30-yr yield target, and Warsh hiked 25 bp unanimously on Sep 16 despite the pressure.
tiles.evidence: The 1951 Accord that freed the Fed from the Treasury followed exactly this pressure, run the other way.

tiles.name: A stated ceiling
tiles.question: Has the Fed announced a cap on long yields?
tiles.trip: Red the day it is said. Amber if yield-curve control enters Fed speeches as an option.
tiles.reading: No FOMC minutes, speeches or Fed statements in the last 30 days mention yield-curve control, yield caps or unlimited purchases as a policy option; Warsh's Aug 28 Jackson Hole speech and Sep 16 presser focused exclusively on fighting inflation, and analysts note the balance-sheet tool exists but Warsh has not floated using it to cap yields.
tiles.evidence: Japan ran a ceiling from 2016; it held only while inflation stayed near zero and domestic savers had nowhere to go. The U.S. ran one from 1942 to 1951.

tiles.name: Expected inflation
tiles.question: Do bond investors expect inflation to stay near 2%?
tiles.trip: Red when 5-year-forward breakevens pass 3%; amber at 2.6%. That is the market naming the policy before the Fed does.
tiles.reading: 5-year, 5-year-forward breakeven 2.34%; 10-year breakeven 2.34% (2026-09-25).
tiles.evidence: Breakevens are the cleanest reading of whether the anchor holds; they stayed anchored through 2021 until they didn't.

tiles.name: Gold against real yields
tiles.question: Is the world buying the one asset that isn't a promise, even while promises pay well?
tiles.trip: Amber when gold is within 3% of its 52-week high while 30-year real yields sit above 2%. Red when gold makes a new high while real yields rise — the referendum going against the pyramid with the odds still in its favor.
tiles.reading: Gold $4,187 (52-week high $5,318); 30-year TIPS real yield 3.21% (+0.52 over three months).
tiles.evidence: Gold has outrun TIPS since 2022 while breakevens stayed flat. It is hedging the regime, not the index.

tiles.name: Foreign demand
tiles.question: Are foreign official holders still showing up for Treasuries?
tiles.trip: Red on a badly tailed coupon auction attributed to foreign absence or a sharp fall in the indirect-bidder share; amber on a falling trend, central-bank gold buying, yuan oil settlement.
tiles.reading: Sep 9 2026 10-yr auction: indirect bidders 79.2%, bid-to-cover 2.71 (solid); Sep 10 30-yr: indirect 79.5%, BTC 2.61; but Sep 15 20-yr: indirect bidders only 52.5%, BTC 2.57, and analysts note primary-dealer share 'somewhat elevated in 2025-26' versus historical averages, consistent with modestly weaker foreign participation.
tiles.evidence: When foreign demand fades, the Fed becomes the marginal buyer whether it wants to or not. That is step one becoming step two by default.
tiles.source: TIC; auction results via web check

tiles.name: The long end
tiles.question: Is the market charging more to hold the government's longest promises?
tiles.trip: Red when the 30-year holds above 5.5% with breakevens unchanged: the premium blowing out on supply alone. Amber above 5%.
tiles.reading: 30-year 5.47% on 2026-09-24; 10-year breakeven +0.03 over three months — a supply premium, not an inflation premium.
tiles.evidence: A long end rising while expected inflation is flat is the market's own yield-curve control, run against the Treasury.

tiles.name: The dollar itself
tiles.question: Is money leaving the dollar, or just leaving bonds?
tiles.trip: Red when the dollar falls more than 5% in a month while long yields rise a quarter point or more — capital leaving the system rather than repricing within it. Amber at 3%.
tiles.reading: Broad dollar index 119.5, +1.0% over a month; 10-year yield +0.54 over the same period.
tiles.evidence: In 2008 and 2020 the dollar rose in the crisis. The day it falls in one is the day the fourth pillar is being tested. April 2025 was the preview.

tiles.name: The arithmetic
tiles.question: Does the debt cost more than the economy grows?
tiles.trip: Red when the 10-year yield exceeds nominal GDP growth; amber within a point of it. Interest costs are shown for scale.
tiles.reading: Nominal GDP growth 6.6% over the year to 2026-04-01; 10-year yield 5.18%; federal interest running at $1,247 billion a year.
tiles.evidence: Every government at this point on the curve has reached for the bond desk. The arithmetic, not the politics, is what forces the steps.

tiles.name: The plumbing door
tiles.question: Is a repo or Treasury-market seizure near enough to give the Fed the financial-stability reason to buy?
tiles.trip: Mirrors the plumbing board: amber while the buffer is gone, red once a seizure is under way. Step two enters through this door.
tiles.reading: Stage 0 of 4 — every ingredient, no event: the buffer is gone and a drain day is near
tiles.evidence: The 2019 spike and the March 2020 seizure were both answered with purchases.

tiles.name: The Fed's own position
tiles.question: Is the Fed politically weaker than it needs to be to keep saying no?
tiles.trip: Red when the Fed's losses or independence become a legislative target, or a dissent for cuts appears from a governor appointed for that purpose.
tiles.reading: As of Mar 25 2026, the Fed's consolidated deferred asset stood at $244 bn (accumulated losses since Sep 2022); the Fed returned to net interest income in late 2025 so the asset is slowly shrinking, but Trump has attempted to remove a governor and the CRS 119th-Congress report flags his 'vocal criticism' and efforts to 'reduce the Fed's independence' as active policy issues.
tiles.evidence: An institution that has to defend its own books is easier to pressure than one that doesn't. The deferred asset is about $230 billion.
tiles.source: Fed financials; Congress via web check

boards.label: Taiwan
boards.title: Taiwan tripwires
boards.summary: 0 tripped, 8 on watch, of 12. No invasion condition present; 3 on watch.

gate.title: No invasion condition present; 3 on watch
gate.text: A blockade or invasion needs three things: a reason (a red line crossed, or Beijing declaring the peaceful path dead), an opening (the U.S. unwilling or tied down, the PLA ready, China's stockpiles full, Taiwan's clock short), and a decision (the mobilization that can't be hidden). Reason plus opening is where the risk lives; a decision means it has started. Only the reason, opening, and decision tiles count here; the markets tile confirms.

parts.name: A reason (red line crossed, or Beijing declares the peaceful path dead)
An opening (U.S. unwilling or tied down, PLA ready, China stocked, Taiwan weak)

groups.title: What would force Xi's hand
groups.blurb: A red line crossed, or Beijing deciding the peaceful path is dead.

groups.title: Whether the window is open
groups.blurb: Capability and opportunity. Three or more of these off green means the door is open.

groups.title: Whether a decision has been made
groups.blurb: The signs that can't be hidden once a move is under way.

tiles.name: Taipei's red lines
tiles.question: Has Taiwan taken a formal step toward independence, or has the U.S. recognized it?
tiles.trip: Trips on a referendum, a constitutional change to name or territory, a declaration, U.S. recognition, or U.S. troops. The one thing that makes a Chinese move near-certain.
tiles.reading: As of Sep 2026, the DPP has not attempted to change the constitution or declare independence; any amendment requires 75% of lawmakers and a referendum threshold Taiwan's divided legislature cannot meet.
tiles.evidence: Written into China's 2005 Anti-Secession Law; every leader since has repeated it.

tiles.tag: Reason: Beijing declares the peaceful path dead
tiles.name: Beijing's language
tiles.question: Has Beijing stopped saying 'peaceful reunification', or declared peaceful means exhausted?
tiles.trip: Trips when Beijing invokes the Anti-Secession Law's third condition or drops the peaceful framing. Amber when the KMT route is failing.
tiles.reading: At the Sep 24 2026 White House summit, Xi pressed Trump to 'oppose' Taiwan independence — stronger wording than the prior US 'do not support' formulation — while Xi's Jan 1 2026 address called reunification 'unstoppable' and established an annual 'Taiwan Recovery Day'; 'peaceful' is still nominally retained but the framing is hardening.
tiles.evidence: The third legal trigger is a judgment call Xi controls — which is exactly why he can wait.

tiles.name: Taiwan's politics
tiles.question: Is Xi's peaceful route — a KMT government in 2028 — still alive?
tiles.trip: Amber if the KMT is losing ground or Beijing's engagement backfires; a DPP win in January 2028 is the hinge.
tiles.reading: Nov 28 2026 local elections are 61 days away; KMT and TPP are cooperating to challenge DPP in all six special municipalities; Xi met KMT chair Cheng Li-wun in Beijing on Apr 10 2026 — the first such meeting in nearly a decade — keeping Beijing's KMT channel alive, but DPP holds the presidency and the 2028 race is wide open, leaving the peaceful route uncertain.
tiles.evidence: January 2028 is the face trap: if the KMT loses after Xi hosted its chair, the peaceful story loses its vehicle.

tiles.name: U.S. commitment
tiles.question: Does Washington look willing and able to fight for Taiwan?
tiles.trip: Amber when arms sales are paused, statements hedge, or carriers are elsewhere; red on an explicit statement of non-defense.
tiles.reading: The USS George Washington was moved out of the Indo-Pacific into CENTCOM by Sep 26 2026, leaving the Far East without a US carrier; a $14 bn arms package has been 'kept in abeyance' since May 2026; Trump at the Sep 24 summit declined to repeat the 'do not support independence' formulation and said only 'He understands how I feel.'
tiles.evidence: The denial strategy is built for this fight; the president has said he made no commitment either way.

tiles.name: PLA readiness
tiles.question: Is the PLA's leadership settled and its amphibious force mature?
tiles.trip: Purges under way are a brake (green). Settled command plus maturing exercises is amber.
tiles.reading: On Jan 24 2026 China's top general Zhang Youxia and Joint Staff chief Liu Zhenli were placed under investigation; CSIS found roughly 68% of deputy theater-command-level officers purged from the command track, creating leadership gaps that analysts say delay any amphibious Taiwan operation, likely pushing the serious window to the late 2020s.
tiles.evidence: You don't fire your commanders on the eve of a war you expect to win.

tiles.name: China's war chest
tiles.question: Are China's oil, grain, and financial reserves being built or drawn down?
tiles.trip: Drawing down (as in 2026) closes the window: green. Refilling fast is amber.
tiles.reading: By end-2025 China held ~1.4 bn barrels of crude in strategic and commercial reserves (~121 days of imports); the EIA assumes China continued building at ~1.0 mn b/d in 2026; gold reserves rose to 2,346 tonnes in Q2 2026 from 2,313 in Q1; no public data on US Treasury selling in the last 30 days.
tiles.evidence: 1.2–1.5 billion barrels bought in 2024–25 is what let China absorb the Iran and Venezuela cuts.

tiles.name: The substitution race
tiles.question: Is China nearing the point where it can absorb a rupture, before the U.S. can?
tiles.trip: Amber as China nears chip sufficiency while U.S. magnet supply is unfinished; the window is 2028–2032.
tiles.reading: China's domestic chip self-sufficiency reached ~28% in Q4 2025 (up from 16% in 2024); SMIC is producing 7nm using multi-patterning DUV; EUV prototype in testing with functional chips targeted 2028–2030; US magnet self-sufficiency still modest — new capacity came online summer 2026 but self-sufficiency 'remains a long road'; the Oct 2025 US–China tech truce was extended only 2 months at the Sep 2026 summit.
tiles.evidence: The side that finishes first gets to choose the break.

tiles.name: Taiwan's own clock
tiles.question: How long could Taiwan last under a blockade, and is it getting longer?
tiles.trip: Red if LNG reserves shrink or the defense budget dies; green only when the clock is visibly lengthening.
tiles.reading: As of mid-2026 Taiwan's LNG reserve stands at ~12 days of consumption and coal at ~40 days (above the statutory 30-day floor); in May 2026 the legislature passed a $24.8 bn 8-year special defense budget, 38% below the executive request; one-year conscription is fully operational as of 2025.
tiles.evidence: Eleven days of gas is the most important number in this whole picture.

tiles.name: Taiwan's will
tiles.question: Do the Taiwanese still say they would fight, and do they believe help is coming?
tiles.trip: Amber if willingness to resist falls below half or trust in the U.S. keeps falling.
tiles.reading: Academia Sinica's Jan 2026 survey (n=1,206) found 58.7% of Taiwanese would resist a Chinese invasion 'at all costs' even without US military help; TVBS found 77% see being pro-US as important; one China principle rejection fell to 58% (from 72–77% in 2019–2023), signalling some softening but still a majority.
tiles.evidence: Giving up is a function of dark cities and whether anyone believes help is coming.

tiles.name: From drills to inspections
tiles.question: Has China moved from exercises to actually stopping ships?
tiles.trip: Trips on any coast-guard boarding or inspection of Taiwan-bound shipping, or a declared quarantine. Drills alone stay green.
tiles.reading: In June 2026 China launched a 'special maritime law enforcement operation' east of Taiwan, hailing three foreign vessels (Singapore, Benin, Liberia-flagged) by radio to demand ship information — no physical boarding occurred but Taiwan's CGA told vessels to ignore the calls; since July China maintains regularized CCG patrols east of Taiwan; CGA counted 244 Chinese vessels in Aug 2026 vs 55 in June; daily PLA aircraft sorties averaged ~7.5 in H1 2026 and ran 3–4 in late Sep 2026.
tiles.evidence: Drills are cheap face; inspections are the first act of a blockade.

tiles.name: Mobilization signs
tiles.question: Is China doing the things a country does in the months before it fights?
tiles.trip: Amber on preparatory steps (ferry requisition drills, reserve call-ups, mobilization-law changes); red on several at once.
tiles.reading: On Aug 28 2026 China's NPC passed a revised National Defense Mobilization Law broadening requisition of civilian assets to 'short-of-war engagements'; by end-2026 China is expected to have built 70+ dual-use RO-RO ferries; a Jan 2026 fishing-fleet L-shaped array of thousands of vessels blocked the Taiwan Strait for 30+ hours; Fuzhou municipal regulations already govern civilian vessel requisition.
tiles.evidence: The mobilization-law revision of August 2026 is one; watch for the rest.

tiles.name: Markets smell it
tiles.question: Are money and insurers pricing a conflict?
tiles.trip: Amber on a 3% fall in the Taiwan dollar in a month, Taiwan stocks lagging the S&P by 8% in 60 sessions, or a sharp insurance move; red at 25% invasion odds or double those moves.
tiles.reading: Taiwan dollar +0.3% vs USD in 30 days; Taiwan ETF vs S&P 500 over 60 sessions +5.2%. Prediction markets: Will China invade Taiwan by September 30, 2026? 0%; Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026? 3%; Will China blockade Taiwan in 2026? 3%; Will China invade Taiwan by June 30, 2027? 8%. No Taiwan-specific war-risk insurance listing or CDS repricing comparable to Hormuz has been reported; Polymarket's 'Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?' contract traded at ~4% as of late Sep 2026 ($42 mn volume); US intelligence community's 2026 Annual Threat Assessment found Chinese leaders have no fixed timeline for unification.
tiles.evidence: Markets price the decision before governments announce it; they also panic for other reasons, so this confirms rather than triggers.
